theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.rule: A value cell on one of this job's five rails is released when its own `source` starts with `@empressaio/setback-corpus@` AND the version between that prefix and the first ':' is strictly older than CORPUS_VERSION, compared component-by-component as int[] (so 1.10.0 sorts ABOVE 1.4.0, and an unreadable version is NOT released, because releasing is a write and an unreadable source is not evidence of staleness). A parcel is released only when EVERY present rail is a state this job may move.
theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.whyThePrefixIsUniqueToThisJob: CORPUS_SOURCE_PREFIX is composed from CORPUS_PACKAGE in exactly one file, and no code line anywhere in src/ types the literal (both asserted against the tree, not in a comment: `the prefix has exactly one producer in src/`). The only other file that composes a corpus source is src/jobs/parcel-envelope-cells.mjs, and its TARGET_RAIL_KEYS are DISJOINT from SETBACK_RAIL_ALLOWLIST -- so no envelope cell can sit on a rail this release reads. Measured on the store: 100% of the value cells on the five rails in the six counties carry this prefix; 0 carry another producer's source.
theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.whereItLives: setbackCellMayBeMoved (pure mirror) and staleCorpusValueGateSql interpolated into UPDATE_SETBACK_CELLS_SQL, so the statement carries the mirror's own expression; PINNED_CORPUS_VERSION_PARAM is derived from CORPUS_VERSION rather than retyped.

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheRelease: The job's own write gate, at the moment the UPDATE is issued. `processCityPage` reads each parcel's prior cell states (PRIOR_SETBACK_CELLS_SQL), calls `staleCorpusReleaseDecision` over them once, and `handleStaleCorpusRelease` either (a) re-stamps -- the same cells with a fresh citation, since the newly built transition's disposition is `value` and no rail's number moved -- (b) writes the pin's new numbers and pushes a valueChanges entry naming every rail's old and new value, or (c) for a parcel whose pinned resolution is not a value, writes the writer's existing district-miss outcome and records the refusal. The SQL that admits the row is `UPDATE_SETBACK_CELLS_SQL`, whose WHERE now has a third alternative, `staleCorpusValueGateSql`, carrying the pure mirror's own expression and comparing against `$6::int[]` derived from CORPUS_VERSION. Executed by: `node src/cli.mjs parcel-setback-cells --county=<fips> [--apply]`, as a Cloud Run Job for any apply (LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN refuses an apply on a laptop).
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: Any run of the job after a corpus pin move -- there is no flag, no switch and no manual step: the pin is `CORPUS_VERSION` in src/lib/setback-writer/setback-table-router.mjs, so as soon as the image's pin is ahead of the version a cell cites, the next run classifies that cell stale. The dispatch's 'any run of the job after a pin move' is exactly right, and it cuts both ways: a pin move with NO run leaves every cell on the old version (named as a bypass below), and a run with no pin move releases nothing (F3, measured 0 on every 1.4.0 cell). A dry run (no --apply) decides and reports without writing; only --apply writes.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenAStaleCorpusValueSurvives: Three things, in the order a reader hits them. (1) The CITATION is false: the cell tells a reader the value came from corpus 1.1.0 while the image's corpus is 1.4.0 -- the class of defect this row exists to end, and the one most-current-source-wins cannot reach. (2) For the six N-CM parcels the VALUE is wrong: 20/5/5/15 against the pinned row's 5/0/0/5, so San Marcos is served a setback the pinned corpus contradicts (today from the bake's legacy-transitional atoms, which is why ruling 19 needs the bake step too). (3) The CONTROLS that fail are the pre-registered prediction comparison and the falsifier suite: a surviving stale population shows up as a mismatch between the run's staleCorpusRestamped/staleCorpusValueChanged and the prediction, as a missing `setback-stale-corpus-release` run_events row where a stale population exists, and -- if the release arm were inert -- as 13 failing tests in test/p363-stale-corpus-release.test.mjs. A gate that silently stopped releasing would not look like an error anywhere; it would look like a smaller number here.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: Named, not hidden: (a) a HAND UPDATE to parcel_record_cell that never runs this job -- nothing in this lane can prevent that, and OPS-19's one-writer-path rule is what bounds it; (b) a SECOND WRITER on the setback rails, which the release cannot distinguish from its own cells EXCEPT by the source prefix: it declines the WHOLE parcel if any present rail is not movable, counts it in staleCorpusBlocked and names the blocking rail, so a foreign rail freezes the set rather than being overwritten -- measured 0 today, and 0-or-loud thereafter; (c) a PIN MOVED WITHOUT A RE-RUN -- the cells keep their old citation until a run happens, and nothing schedules that run, so the pin move and the release are two separate human acts; (d) a source the rule cannot READ is deliberately not released (a malformed version is a bypass by design: a write never rides on an unreadable input); (e) the release re-resolves with the cell's own recorded (jurisdictionKey, districtCode), so a parcel whose LIVE zoning district changed since its setback cells were written keeps the old code until the zoning rail's own change lands -- deliberate, and named in the job header; (f) the envelope writer's cells cite the same corpus but sit on disjoint rails, and the disjointness is asserted rather than assumed.
